text: In one screen A coding harness such as Claude Code ( Claude Code, taken apart ) is invoked : you open a session in a repository, it works, the session ends.

text: A personal agent is resident : a background program that never ends, receives messages on the chat apps you already use, wakes itself on a timer to check whether anything needs doing, keeps notes about you for months, and acts on your accounts (mail, calendar, payments) rather than on a repository.
label: core

text: Inside, it runs the same agent loop the parent page teaches ( Topic: agentic-harnesses , Reading section 1).
label: core

text: What changes is everything around the loop: who can write into its context, what authority it holds while nobody watches, and what can check or undo its work.
label: core

text: Coding harness (Claude Code, Codex CLI) Personal agent (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent) How a run starts You start a session A message, a timer (heartbeat), a scheduled job or a webhook How long state lives One session, plus memory files you keep Months: a searchable session history, memory files the agent itself edits, a profile of you What it acts on A repository and a terminal Your accounts: chat, mail, calendar, browser, sometimes payments and devices Who is watching Usually you, at the terminal Often nobody: a heartbeat or a scheduled job runs while you sleep Who writes into its context Mostly you, plus files you chose to open Anyone who can send you a message or an email: the input channel is open to third parties by design What checks the work Tests, compiler, CI, a diff you review Usually nothing automatic: "was my inbox handled well?" has no test suite Undo Git: nearly everything is revertible A sent message, a booking or a payment usually cannot be taken back Permissions Per-tool approval inside a session you watch Standing access to live accounts, granted once at setup Synthesised from the two projects' docs and the coding-harness pages below; every row is argued, with sources, in the sections it points to (1, 4 to 7).

text: Four layers that can be swapped separately OpenClaw separates the provider (who serves the model), the model (written provider/model , split on the first slash, so openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k2 works), the agent runtime (who runs the loop) and the channel (where messages enter and leave) DOCUMENTED ( agent runtimes ).
label: depth

text: The runtime layer is the interesting one for this topic: Embedded harnesses run inside OpenClaw's own prepared loop: the built-in openclaw runtime, plus plugin runtimes codex and copilot (the latter opt-in, never picked automatically).
label: depth

text: External harnesses attach over ACP (the Agent Client Protocol): "Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, and similar external harnesses still use ACP." For a runtime it does not own, the docs ask a fixed list of compatibility questions: who owns the model loop, who owns the canonical thread history, whether OpenClaw's own tools and its before_tool_call / after_tool_call hooks still fire, whether the context-engine lifecycle runs, what compaction data is exposed, and what is intentionally unsupported.

section: 4. messages that arrive while the agent is working
text: Four policies (OpenClaw's names): steer : put the message into the current run at the next safe boundary, so the model reads it before its next decision; followup (Hermes calls it queue ): finish the current run, then run the message as a new turn; collect : like followup, but merge several queued messages into one later turn after a short wait; interrupt : abort the current run and start again with the new message.
label: core

section: 4. messages that arrive while the agent is working
text: Exactly where the boundary is.
label: fat

section: 4. messages that arrive while the agent is working
text: OpenClaw steers by default.
label: core

section: 4. messages that arrive while the agent is working
text: It never interrupts a tool that is already running; in a reply with several sequential tool calls it starts the first one without checking, then checks before each later one and skips the rest with a synthetic result ("Skipped to process an incoming message."); after the batch settles "it appends the exact drained steering messages after the tool results, before the next LLM call"; parallel batches are never skipped DOCUMENTED ( queue steering ).
label: core
key: Skipped to process an incoming message.

section: 4. messages that arrive while the agent is working
text: Hermes defaults to a redirecting interrupt: "messaging a busy agent redirects its active turn (a running foreground terminal command is moved to the background rather than killed, so your message is read immediately)", applied "at the next tool-result boundary"; queue and steer are options, /stop is a hard stop DOCUMENTED ( Hermes messaging ).
label: core
key: moved to the background rather than killed
